title: Dynamic Regression / ARIMAX
interviewAnswer: Dynamic regression combines external predictors with time-series error structure. It is useful when known drivers such as price, holidays or weather explain demand but residuals remain autocorrelated.
keyPoints: Future exogenous variables must be known or forecast.
Scenario forecasts depend on driver scenarios.
why: Dynamic Regression / ARIMAX appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Future exogenous variables must be known or forecast.
deepDive: Dynamic regression combines external predictors with time-series error structure. It is useful when known drivers such as price, holidays or weather explain demand but residuals remain autocorrelated. Residual autocorrelation indicates incomplete dynamics. Scenario forecasts depend on driver scenarios. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Forecast energy demand using temperature and calendar variables with ARIMA errors.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Dynamic Regression / ARIMAX make?
How would you validate or debug Dynamic Regression / ARIMAX in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
